evals.name: large-target-fan-out
evals.prompt: Run a full code quality audit of services/billing.
evals.expected_output: Measures authored lines with the git ls-files count, splits the target into package batches when it is over ~20k lines, starts one code-quality-auditor per batch in a single message, then merges the reports into one with combined coverage and a single verdict.
expectations: Measures the target's authored line count before choosing a split
Starts all code-quality-auditor calls in one message so they run in parallel
Gives each auditor the target path and its batch of packages
Merges the reports into one: duplicates removed, a pattern found in several batches combined into one finding with every location
Ends with one coverage list and a single verdict, and edits no files

evals.name: small-target-single-auditor
evals.prompt: Can you do a quality pass on services/api?
evals.expected_output: Measures the target; if it is under ~10k authored lines, starts a single code-quality-auditor on the whole of services/api rather than splitting it, and relays its report.
expectations: Measures the target's authored line count before choosing a split
Uses one auditor for a target under ~10k lines instead of splitting by package

evals.name: no-target-named
evals.prompt: Audit the code quality of this repo.
evals.expected_output: Asks which subproject to audit instead of picking one or auditing the whole monorepo.
expectations: Asks the user to name a subproject path
Does not start any auditor before a target is named

evals.name: flags-nesting-and-cycle
evals.prompt: Do a code quality audit of services/orders.
evals.expected_output: Starts one auditor whose prompt carries the skill's criteria verbatim. The report flags order_total in orders/pricing.py as about 60 lines, nested six levels deep and well above complexity 7, proposing pure functions in place of the nested blocks, and flags the orders.models <-> orders.pricing import cycle with both edges, proposing that the Order and Line types sit below the pricing functions.
expectations: Passes the criteria section to the auditor in its prompt
Flags order_total in orders/pricing.py for exceeding the 80x24 box, with its line count
Flags order_total for cyclomatic complexity above about 7 and its deep nesting, and proposes replacing nested blocks with calls to pure functions
Flags the dependency cycle between orders.models and orders.pricing, naming both edges
Proposes breaking the cycle by keeping the types below the pricing functions, for example by removing Order.total, rather than adding an interface layer
